findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_wait_reports can request a reset after 100000 consecutive unchanged millisecond readings. No execution-time bound establishes that this count cannot be reached within one healthy timer tick. SWC-SUP-002 permits the barrier to end on report completion, failure notification, or watchdog reset after transmission stops progressing.
findings.requested_change: Establish a valid progress-based termination rule and its timing bounds, or obtain an upstream decision that permits the implemented reset behavior.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_run returns immediately when fm_is_latched() is true after only one dc_service_step(). On a watchdog reset with an already-set latch, the queued RST and code 8 lines can remain incomplete, although SWC-SUP-002 and SWR-RST-003 require the watchdog-reset report.
findings.requested_change: Keep the latched start-up path servicing the required messages through completion or an explicitly permitted failure or reset outcome, without releasing application tasks.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_submit discards a report when the 36-entry pending queue is full. SWC-SUP-008 requires each detection to be submitted for reporting within 10 ms, but the design does not establish that arrivals and drain time prevent overflow or late submission.
findings.requested_change: Provide an implementable admission and transmission strategy with justified arrival and timing bounds that meets the reporting requirements; resolve OP-SWC-013 where a product decision is necessary.

findings.description: SWC-SUP-061 and OP-SWC-011 leave the T_DIAG flow rule unresolved: the design checks at the 5 ms cycle-end phase, although T_DIAG may be within its 20 ms execution limit. A timely execution can therefore be reported as a missing checkpoint.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision and align the flow and timing design with it.

findings.description: SWU-TIM-001 now counts from timer value zero, but OP-SWU-014 records that the inputs do not establish that the target timer runs from reset or that hal_timer_start preserves it. The design therefore does not establish the reset-relative timestamp required by SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003.
findings.requested_change: Establish a supported reset-relative time source and its initialization contract, or resolve the missing platform fact before relying on it.
